content: Hi, I'm an experimental physicist with an undergrad degree in eng. physics and a minor in math; I'm new to Lean but intrigued. My interests are definitely more towards analysis, physics, linear algebra, and similar topics. Is there a good first issue you'd all recommend to learn the process for contributing? Nice to meet you all.
I did see that Green's theorem was missing from the 100 theorems list, which seemed like an interesting project to me.

Hey @A. Young ! Nice to meet you! Lots of physics happening over on #Physlib > New members (this is one of the channels on here you have to actively subscribe to) which you might be interested in! We also have lots of TODOs which would be good for beginners.

@Joseph Tooby-Smith Yes, I'd subscribed to that. I took a look at the TODOs which seem a little all over the place and in one of the physlib threads it seemed like it might be out of date, so wasn't sure. Do you know if mathlib has formalized anything to do with multivectors yet, out of curiosity?

TODOs should be up-to-date now. If you have any suggestions on how to make them clearer/easier to understand that would be very much appreciated. Mathlib have exterior algebras which I think is related to what you mean by Multivectors.
